svg.text: Solderable breadboard layout: two-motor wall piece with a Seeed XIAO ESP32-S3 (top view)
Half-size breadboard-style board, 30 columns. In each column rows a-e are joined, and rows f-j are joined; the two halves are not. Not built or tested.
header in row a; the board hangs
over the top edge (size not checked).
24 V and the motor go to
header in row a; the board hangs
over the top edge (size not checked).
24 V and the motor go to
Wire list (all jumpers lie on top of the board; hole = column, row)
Driver 1 header on columns 1-10: VDD 1, GND 2, DIR 3, STEP 4, MS1 5, MS2 6, DIAG 7, INDEX 8, UART 9, EN 10. Driver 2 on columns 11-20, same order.
3V3 rail: from e1, e11, e21 (the two VDD pins and the pull-up end) and from XIAO 3V3 (j27). GND rail: from e2, e12 (driver GND pins) and XIAO GND (j28).
STEP 1: e4 to XIAO D0 (GPIO1, col 29) DIR 1: d3 to XIAO D1 (GPIO2, col 28) STEP 2: d14 to XIAO D3 (GPIO4, col 26) DIR 2: e13 to XIAO D4 (GPIO5, col 25)
EN: c10 to c20 (joins both EN pins), then b20 to XIAO D5 (GPIO6, col 24). Pull-up: 10k stood upright between column 20 (EN) and column 21 (3V3).
MS1, MS2, DIAG, INDEX, UART: nothing connected. XIAO D2 (GPIO3) left free: it is a boot strapping pin. D8 to D10 (GPIO7 to 9) are free for a third motor or the Hall sensors.
24 V never touches it. The Wago blocks feed each driver's + and GND screw terminals directly (100 uF across each), and each motor lead goes to that driver's 1A/1B/2A/2B screws.
The XIAO runs from its USB-C only. The USB-C panel cable and the right-end motor lead leave through the RIGHT end wall, the DC jack and left motor lead through the LEFT end wall.
1. XIAO orientation: the pin names are drawn for USB-C pointing right with the pins in rows e and i (6 holes apart). Confirm against the Seeed pin chart for your board.
2. Driver header order (VDD, GND, DIR, STEP, MS1, MS2, DIAG, INDEX, UART, EN) is from Adafruit's photo. Read the silkscreen on your board, and which way the board faces.
3. Solder female sockets for the XIAO and for each driver's header, then plug them in. Use hot glue or a standoff so a driver is not carried by its 10 pins alone.
4. Arduino IDE: board 'XIAO_ESP32S3' and set USB CDC On Boot to Enabled, or the serial commands and the control panel will not work.
5. For the single test unit, fit driver 1 and its jumpers only; the same pins work, with NUM_MOTORS set to 1.
